# Tidepool Landing Page: Build Plan

**Visual system:** Warm off-white (#F6F3EC) base, deep slate-teal ink (#1E3A3F), tide-blue accent (#3B7EA1), and sand (#E8D9BC) for panels. Headlines in a geometric sans; body in a humanist sans; one serif for the pull quote. All imagery is real product screenshots, not stock.

**1. Nav bar**
Left: wordmark. Center: Features, How it works, Pricing. Right: "Log in" text link and a filled "Start a week" button. Sticky, with a thin border on scroll.

**2. Hero**
Two columns. Left: headline "Plan the week together, before Monday starts," a one-line subhead naming the buyer (small teams of 2–15), a primary button "Start free," and a secondary "See a sample week." Right: a tilted screenshot of a shared week board with three avatars and live cursors.

**3. Problem strip**
Full-width sand band with three short statements: "Plans live in five chat threads." "Someone always double-books." "Monday starts with a meeting about the meeting." Sans-serif, 20px, no icons.

**4. Shared week view (feature 1)**
Full-bleed screenshot of a horizontal Mon–Sun grid with one lane per teammate. Left-aligned headline "Everyone's week on one page." Three sentences max. Caption-style annotation pointing to a conflict flag.

**5. Dependencies (feature 2)**
Reversed layout: text right, diagram left. Thin tide-blue connector lines link tasks across days and owners. Headline: "See what waits on what." Copy names a concrete example: "Design review Thursday unlocks Friday's launch."

**6. Monday ritual (feature 3)**
Three-column card row: "Review," "Commit," "Share." Each card has one sentence and a small checklist mockup. Headline: "Plan in ten minutes."

**7. Customer proof**
Sand background. One large serif pull quote with name, role, and team size. Below it, a row of grayscale customer wordmarks (only with permission).

**8. How it works**
Vertical three-step sequence with numbers 1–3: create the week, invite the team, commit by Friday. Thin connecting line between steps. Under 40 words total.

**9. Pricing**
Two tiers: Team (free up to 5 people) and Studio (unlimited). Plain feature lists, no "most popular" badge, annual toggle. Headline: "Pay per team, not per seat."

**10. FAQ**
Five accordion items: integrations, data export, team size limits, admin controls, cancellation.

**11. Closing CTA**
Full-width tide-blue block. Headline: "Start next Monday ready." Single button, no email field.

**12. Footer**
Four columns: product, company, resources, legal. Small wordmark and a sea-glass line illustration.

# Tidepool Landing Page: Revised Build Plan

**What changed:** The hero now states a specific outcome instead of a vague benefit. Proof appears above the fold instead of near the bottom. Overlapping sections are merged, and the page adds an objection-handling FAQ and a clearer pricing rationale. The page does not reuse the reference's shopping-list elements (week-timeline sidebar, hand-drawn arrow, forest and coral palette, long run-on hero), since those belong to a different product.

**Visual system:** Warm off-white (#F6F3EC) base, deep slate-teal ink (#1E3A3F), tide-blue accent (#3B7EA1), sand (#E8D9BC) for panels. Geometric sans for headlines, humanist sans for body, one serif reserved for quotes. All imagery is real product screenshots with real-looking team data, never stock.

**1. Nav bar**
Wordmark left. Features, How it works, Pricing centered. "Log in" text link and a filled "Start free" button right. Sticky with a thin border on scroll.

**2. Hero**
Two columns. Headline: "Plan your team's week in one shared view." Subhead: "Tidepool shows who owns what, what's blocked, and what's due, so Monday starts with a plan." Primary button "Start free," secondary "See a sample week." Right: screenshot of the shared week board with three avatars and a visible conflict flag.

**3. Proof strip**
Directly under the hero. Four grayscale customer wordmarks (with permission) and one metric: "Teams plan their week in 14 minutes on average." Only include the metric once verified.

**4. Problem**
Sand band, three statements in sans-serif, with a stake for each: "Plans live in five chat threads. Double-bookings surface on Wednesday. Monday opens with a meeting about the meeting." No icons.

**5. Shared week view (feature 1)**
Full-bleed screenshot of a Mon–Sun grid, one lane per teammate. Headline: "Everyone's week, on one page." Three sentences max. One annotation callout on a double-booking, labeled in plain language, not a decorative arrow.

**6. Dependencies (feature 2)**
Reversed layout: diagram left, text right. Tide-blue connector lines link tasks across days and owners. Headline: "See what waits on what." Concrete example in the copy: "Design review Thursday unlocks Friday's launch. If review slips, you'll know before Friday."

**7. Monday ritual (feature 3)**
Three cards: Review, Commit, Share. One sentence and one small checklist mockup each. Headline: "Plan in ten minutes." Include a "Run it yourself" link to a template.

**8. Customer proof**
Sand background. One large serif pull quote with name, role, and team size, plus one specific outcome ("We stopped the Thursday status call"). Only quotes approved by the customer.

**9. How it works**
Three numbered steps with a thin connecting line: create the week, invite the team, commit by Friday. Under 40 words total. Short enough to scan in five seconds.

**10. Pricing**
Two tiers: Team (free up to 5 people) and Studio (unlimited people, per team). Plain feature lists, annual toggle, no "most popular" badge. Headline: "Pay per team, not per seat." Subline: "Adding a fifth person won't change your bill unless you move to Studio."

**11. FAQ**
Six accordion items, answering the real objections: "Is this another app to check?", integrations, data export, admin controls, security, cancellation. Each answer is two sentences or fewer.

**12. Closing CTA**
Full-width tide-blue block. Headline: "Start next Monday ready." Primary "Start free" button and a secondary "Book a 15-minute setup" link. No email field.

**13. Footer**
Four columns: product, company, resources, legal. Small wordmark and a sea-glass line illustration.

**Cross-cutting requirements**
- **Mobile:** Stack the week grid into a day-by-day scroll. Keep the hero CTA above the fold.
- **Accessibility:** Meet WCAG AA contrast on all sand and tide-blue text. Every screenshot needs alt text describing the data shown.
- **Measurement:** Track hero CTA clicks, pricing toggle use, and sample-week views as the primary funnel.
